correctness.rationale: For S⊆∏[n_i], to realize S\{x} but not x requires x to be a strictly largest coordinate among S in some i; conversely the coordinate maxima of any desired T⊆S then exclude every y outside T by its private maximum. Each coordinate has either one private maximum label or none; for prescribed j labels the count of m-coordinate tuples avoiding them is n_i^m−j∑_{v=1}^{n_i}(v−1)^{m−1}. Inclusion-exclusion divided by m! gives s_m, with no repeated successful points. At m≥2 each nontrivial coordinate supports at most one label and independent two-level witnesses give VCdim max(1,r). For q_m-alphabet samples each coordinate emits label a with probability p_m=A_m(q_m)/q_m^m≤1/m; Bonferroni with d_mp_m=log m+c+o(1), d_mp_m²→0 proves exp(−exp(−c)), and collision probability is o(1). Handles m=1, n_i=1, zero trace, and arbitrary changing alphabets.

value.rationale: Principal order ideals of finite products of chains are a canonical finite geometric range space; an all-coefficient count, not merely VCdim, measures its complete shattering complex. The sampling theorem supplies a natural sharp, model-relevant dimension transition between Boolean and large alphabets. Arbitrary grid dimensions and alphabet lengths prevent an artificial finite slice.

final_claim: All finite products of chains with anchored lower principal orthants have a strict private-maximum shattering criterion, an all-degree inclusion-exclusion support polynomial, exact VC dimension max(1,#nontrivial chains), and an alphabet-dependent random-support coupon-collector Gumbel threshold.
limitations: Only finite anchored coordinatewise lower orthants, not unrestricted rectangles, all order ideals, or generic higher-order range families; Gumbel limit is random uniform subset with arbitrary q_m≥2, not a uniform finite-size approximation.
residual_risks: An unindexed monotone-conjunction or principal-order-ideal counting theorem could use the same strict-coordinate-max characterization.
